# Sikkhāpadavibhaṅga (Vb 14)

**ID:** Vb 14
**Section:** Vibhaṅga (vb)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Sikkhāpadavibhaṅga
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh02m.mul13.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Unlike many other chapters of the *Vibhaṅga*, the *Sikkhāpadavibhaṅga* lacks a Sutta-explanation section (*suttantabhājanīya*) and consists solely of an Abhidhamma-explanation (*abhidhammabhājanīya*) followed by a catechetical interrogation (*pañhāpucchaka*) [Hazra 1994; Nyanatiloka 1983].

In the Abhidhamma section, after the individual precepts are defined, the inquiry broadens to examine training in general (*katame dhammā sikkhā*) [Nyanatiloka 1983]. This is answered by outlining formulas for all classes of wholesome consciousness (*kusala-citta*) across the sensuous, fine-material, immaterial, and supramundane spheres, demonstrating that all three higher trainings (*sikkhā*)—morality, concentration, and wisdom—can be systematically formulated in terms of consciousness [Nyanatiloka 1983]. The concluding catechetical section subjects the five precepts to the Abhidhamma matrix, establishing that they are invariably karmically wholesome, mundane, tied to karmic results, and pertain to limited, external sense objects [Nyanatiloka 1983].

 DharmaNexus corroborates this relationship, registering cross-language matches with the Sanskrit *Dharmaskandha* as well as alignments with the *Ādikarmapradīpa*, *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā*, and the Sanskrit *Ekottarāgama* [DharmaNexus]. Internally, DharmaNexus records 3,535 matching text-reuse passages across 102 Pali texts, sharing extensive material with other *Vibhaṅga* treatises (notably the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga*, *Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga*, and *Appamaññāvibhaṅga*) and consciousness classifications in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* [DharmaNexus].
